feedback: Evidence: iterations 0 to 3 all ended off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m on every track, regardless of span (±0.024 vs ±0.05 m), footprint (12 vs 16 mm) or kp (3.0 vs 3.5), so none of these set the excursion. Iteration 1 removed line loss on oval and slalom by widening the span. Iteration 2 (16 mm, ±0.05 m, y 0.04, kp 3.5, ki 0) is still the best at 26.99. Iteration 3 changed y to 0.06 and added ki 0.3 at once: line loss returned on s-bend and slalom and max_error stayed at 0.061 m, so the look-ahead and integral change did not help. Before the next race, two points on wheel_track. First, yaw rate is the wheel-speed difference divided by wheel_track, so widening the track reduces yaw per unit of steering command. Your 'more turning authority' is therefore likely to act as less steering gain, and I compensate with kp 4.4 in the package, which keeps the effective gain equal to iteration 2. Second, the excursion is identical across tracks, so it may be a start-up transient or a fixed bias rather than a corner-tracking limit. The outcome of this race is unknown. Hold the best-known geometry (16 mm, ±0.05 m, y 0.04) and read the wheel_track result alongside max_error. If max_error still sits at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, the excursion does not respond to track or gain, and the next test should be mass (lighter, about 0.6 kg, to reduce yaw inertia) or a change in the start-up geometry. If line loss returns at 0.15 m, revert the track to 0.12 m.
requested_changes: Keep the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m and y = 0.04 m (iteration 2 geometry), and test wheel_track 0.15 m as the single geometry change; report max_error and line_loss_events per track.
If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, try mass 0.6 kg (lower yaw inertia) with the same sensors, leaving wheel_track as the best result shows.
If line loss returns at wheel_track 0.15 m, revert to 0.12 m and hold the iteration-2 geometry, since y = 0.06 already reintroduced line loss.
